newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Oil Search output/revenue falls in Mch qtr.
newsitem.headline: Oil Search output/revenue falls in Mch qtr.

text.p: Papua New Guinea oil and gas producer Oil Search Ltd said on Wednesday it posted operating revenue for the March quarter of A$17.83 million, down from A$20.35 million in the December quarter.

Oil Search's share of crude oil production declined to 616,500 barrels, or 6,850 barrels per day (bpd) from 708,200 barrels, or 7,698 bpd, previously as a result of a natural decline in the Kutubu fields, the company said.
Oil Search's share of gas production from the Hides project totalled 63.7 milliion cubic feet for the quarter, up marginally from 61.3 million in the December quarter.
Oil Search said its average realised oil price fell to US$22.07 a barrel in the March quarter from $US22.59 in the previous three month period.
Average oil production at Kutubu, in which Oil Search has a 7.763 percent stake, was 89,229 bpd in the quarter.
Oil production at Kutubu decreased slightly as a result of natural field decline, Oil Search said.
A number of workovers conducted in the quarter were successful in reducing field decline, it said.
Oil Search said a development drilling campaign would begin at Kutubu in June 1997.
"A series of wells are planned to add production capacity to the fields and an increase in oil production is expected in the second half of 1997," the company said in its quarterly report.

"Work also commenced in the quarter to increase gas comparison capacity in the fields. Increased oil production of between 2,000 and 3,000 barrels of oil per day is expected when restaging of the compressors is complete," it said.
